## 1. Learn Page/Screen Files

There are **four key source files** that make up the Learn page:

### A. Learn Main Screen (the page that lists all courses/modules)
**`/workspaces/learn-p5/src/app/learn/index.tsx`** (163 lines)

This is the primary Learn screen. It exports a `Learn` component that:
- Loads all courses via `loadAllCourses()` from the course loader utility
- Loads completed lessons and completed courses from AsyncStorage
- Renders a `FlatList` of `ExerciseCard` components (one per course)
- Orders courses: active (incomplete) first, then completed courses
- Determines which course is the "current" (first incomplete) one

Key rendering snippet (lines 72-121):
```tsx
<Header title="Learn" />
<FlatList
  style={styles.flatList}
  contentContainerStyle={{ paddingBottom: 32 }}
  ListHeaderComponent={
    <Text style={[styles.sectionTitle, { color: derivedColors.primary }]}>
      Courses
    </Text>
  }
  data={orderedCourses}
  keyExtractor={(item) => item.slug}
  renderItem={({ item }) => {
    const completed = isCourseCompleted(item);
    const isCurrent = currentSlug === item.slug;
    const locked = !completed && !isCurrent;
    return (
      <View style={styles.cardWrapper}>
        <ExerciseCard
          title={item.title}
          moduleName={item.moduleName}
          description={`${item.exercises.length} exercise${...} · ${item.description}`}
          locked={locked}
          completed={completed}
          isCurrent={isCurrent}
          onContinue={() => router.push(`/learn/${item.slug}`)}
        />
      </View>
    );
  }}
/>
```

### B. Learn Layout (Stack navigator for the Learn section)
**`/workspaces/learn-p5/src/app/learn/_layout.tsx`** (10 lines)

A simple Expo Router `Stack` layout with two screens: `index` (the main list) and `[course]` (course detail pages). No `headerShown` -- headers are custom.

### C. Course Detail Screen

The screen shown when a user taps a course/module. It renders:
- Breadcrumbs ("Learn" > course title)
- A "Next exercise" hero section with a progress bar

- "Completed" section (faded, opacity 0.3)

## 2. How Modules Are Listed and Styled

Modules are **not** rendered by a separate "ModuleList" component. Instead, courses (which serve as the concept of "modules") are displayed as cards in a `FlatList` on the Learn screen. Each course/card uses the `ExerciseCard` component.

### The `ExerciseCard` Component
**`/workspaces/learn-p5/src/components/ExerciseCard.tsx`** (112 lines)

Each card displays:
- **Icon area** (top, large): 48x48 SVG asterisk or a lock/check icon, centered with `paddingVertical: 40`
- **Content area** (below icon):
  - `title` (fontSize 24, bold)
  - `moduleName` (fontSize 11, uppercase, primary color)
  - `description` (fontSize 16, secondary color, or locked message)
- **Button** (bottom, conditional): "Continue" button shown only for the current (active) course

## 4. Supporting Files

### Course Data Types
**`/workspaces/learn-p5/src/data/types.ts`** (42 lines)

Defines the `Course` interface:
```ts
export interface Course {
  slug: string;        // unique identifier, e.g. "shapes"
  title: string;       // display title, e.g. "Shapes"
  moduleName: string;  // group/category, e.g. "Fundamentals"
  description: string; // short description
  exercises: Exercise[];
}
```

### Course Loader
**`/workspaces/learn-p5/src/utils/courseLoader.ts`** (60 lines)

Imports all 16 course data objects and exposes `loadAllCourses()` and `loadCourse(slug)`.

### Module Progress Hook
**`/workspaces/learn-p5/src/hooks/useModuleProgress.ts`** (48 lines)

A small hook that manages `completedCourses` in AsyncStorage and provides:
- `isModuleUnlocked(moduleName)` -- checks if a module/course is unlocked
- `getLockedCourseName(moduleName, currentCourseSlug)` -- returns which course needs to be completed first
- `markCourseCompleted(courseSlug)` -- persists completion

### Course YAML Data Files (16 courses)
Located at `/workspaces/learn-p5/src/data/courses/*.yaml`. Each has a `moduleName` field that groups related courses (e.g., both `shapes.yaml` and `color.yaml` have `moduleName: "Fundamentals"`). This `moduleName` is displayed on the `ExerciseCard` and in the course detail screen.
